target_customer: Fleet operators who need to pay and track parking tickets, municipalities, and drivers paying for parking without accounts
problem: Drivers and fleets struggle to pay for parking and find and pay tickets; fleets lose track of tickets and compliance.
business_model: Transaction fees on parking payments plus fleet and municipal software

founders.name: Jim Gibbs
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a software developer by trade focused on business pain points.

founders.name: Daniel Lopretto
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CTO on the YC page; Technical.ly summary reports him as co-founder.

investors: Google for Startups Black Founders Fund

competitors.name: Passport
competitors.what: Mobile parking payment and enforcement software for cities
competitors.traction_then: Said it had systems in over 1,000 locations in 46 states and provinces

technical_complexity.rationale: GPS based parking payment on top of existing city payment systems is mostly integration work with municipalities rather than novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: City contracts such as the Pittsburgh Parking Authority deal take years, but payment apps are copyable and ParkMobile and Passport were already in cities.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept expanding city by city in 2016; no copying or acquisition of Meter Feeder was found. It survived and pivoted toward fleets and autonomous vehicle payments.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in March 2016 covered the launch as a way to ditch coins and codes. Cities were rolling out app payments through 2016 (ParkNYC in December 2016), showing demand for mobile parking payment.

brand_strength.rationale: Local press in Pittsburgh and Black founder coverage exist, but no source shows brand driven growth. Search results blur with an unrelated company named Meter.

pivots.from: Pay for parking with GPS for drivers
pivots.to: Fleet ticket payment and machine to machine parking payments for autonomous vehicles
pivots.why: YC description now says fleets; site says first machine to machine municipal payments by autonomous vehicles. Dates not stated.

outcome_analysis: Meter Feeder stayed small, with 4 people on the YC page and a plan to grow from nine to 15 in 2022. It raised a 2.6 million dollar seed extension in April 2022 and signed the Pittsburgh Parking Authority rollout in 2021 after the pandemic delayed a 2019 negotiation. It is active, with a 2026 autonomous vehicle payment milestone. Growth has been slow and capital light.
notes: Total raised before April 2022 was reported as over 1 million dollars (2021 launch article) and 2.3 million dollars (Technical.ly Sept 2021); earlier rounds not found, so coverage is partial. CB Insights lists 3.27 million over 8 rounds, inconsistent, unverified. The Black Founders Fund grant amount is up to 100,000 per founder, not stated for this company. Only one competitor with a dated source was found; ParkMobile 2016 city launches were seen in search results but the specific page for each was not opened.
